correctness.rationale: On each size class the label action is transitive, so independent exchangeable matchings become independent uniform matchings given their sizes. Counting completions of r prescribed disjoint edges in size b gives 2^r (b)_r/(n)_{2r}; summing over the binom(a,r) subsets of the first matching proves the exact PGF including empty size classes of positive probability. For the circle, root the cyclic order at a sampled label; the spacings are Dirichlet(1,...,1) and their order is that of iid exponentials. The shortest direction from a point meets an adjacent point first; hence reciprocal edges are exactly strict cyclic gap minima. Their mean is 1/3, adjacent joint probability 0 and distance-two joint probability 2/15 (integrate independent uniform gap ranks x,y with factor (1-x)(1-y)(1-max(x,y))); triples farther apart are independent. This gives the stated mean and variance for n>=5 and a stationary two-dependent CLT after changing at most two seam terms. Given M_i the two overlaps sharing sample i are independent and have means 2R_i/[3(n-1)], which gives the finite covariance. For the joint factorial-moment expansion, in a pattern with m distinct prescribed edges, v distinct label vertices, and D required incidences of a prescribed edge in a particular matching, the contribution is O(n^{v-D}) or zero if matching constraints conflict. Always v<=2m and D>=2m. A shared vertex makes the first strict; reuse of an entire edge across distinct pair types makes the second strict. The remaining configurations have (n)_{2T}/2^T assignments for T ordered slots and tend to the product factorial moments of independent Poisson variables of means 2 rho_i rho_j. These estimates hold along every deterministic size sequence tending to the stated ratios, with uniformly bounded moments for each fixed multi-index. The product Poisson law is moment-determinate. With random sizes whose ratios tend in probability to 1/3 the conditional expectations of bounded overlap test functions therefore tend in probability to constants, giving joint independence from the Gaussian size vector.
residual_risks: No uploaded checker was executed. The limiting argument treats fixed q, not a growing number of occasions. The circular spacing assertion is for a cyclic order rooted at a sampled point rather than at an external coordinate origin.

evidence: Deng gives total-variation approximation by independent Poissons for hits of deterministic edge-disjoint bounded-degree targets by a uniform perfect matching; §5 partitions overlapping target edge sets by membership. Spiro–Surya supplies the earlier marginal full-matching overlap context.

Bahadır–Ceyhan gives n/3, 2n/45 and the normalized Gaussian limit for reflexive pairs in the uniform interval model. The interval counts one-sided minima at the two ends of the path of n-1 gaps; for circular ranks one may use the same iid ranks, add the nth gap and change only the two end tests.

evidence: For deterministic sizes s_i/n tending to rho_i, expose uniform partial matchings one at a time. At step i let the earlier partial matchings be targets. Their pairwise common-edge counts are O_p(1), since the exact inclusion mean is 2s_js_k/[n(n-1)]. Deleting these multiply listed target edges changes a uniform perfect matching's hit vector with probability o(1), by its 1/(N-1) single-edge hit probability. The remaining targets have degree at most one and size s_j-o_p(n); their perfect-matching hit counts converge conditionally to independent Pois(rho_j) by Deng applied along deterministic target sequences.

The hit vector is tight. Conditional on boundedly many hit edges, a uniformly chosen s_i-edge subset of the floor(n/2) real edges retains them asymptotically as independent Bernoulli(2rho_i) marks, from the finite hypergeometric law. Thus the overlap block at exposure i has conditional product Poisson limit with means 2rho_i rho_j, independent in the limit of the past. Iteration over fixed q gives all pair coordinates; convergence along every deterministic size sequence gives the same conditional limit for random circular sizes and hence independence from their Gaussian fluctuations.

The residual finite positive covariance is Var(R_i) multiplied by the two unconditional single-edge probabilities in replicates j,k. This follows directly because given M_i the two overlaps are independent with conditional means proportional to R_i.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The conditional Poisson vector and its decoupling, not merely one marginal, follow from the stronger approximation by this exposure/thinning transfer. Together with the exact PGF transfer, the known local-minimum CLT and elementary conditional-covariance calculation, this leaves no supported distinct substantive claim at the frozen scope.

evidence: Given the sizes, fix the first partial matching as a deterministic disjoint-edge target and use a uniform size-b partial matching for the second. Let N be n rounded up to even. Form it by choosing uniformly b of the floor(n/2) edges of a uniform perfect matching on N labels after removing the dummy-incident edge if n is odd. Permutation invariance proves uniformity on the size-b class.

Deng Lemma 3.3 with a single size-a matching target gives PGF coefficient binom(a,r) 2^r (N/2)_r/(N)_{2r} on (z-1)^r for the unthinned intersection. Conditional on any unthinned intersection count h, the retained count is hypergeometric with factorial moments (h)_r (b)_r/(floor(n/2))_r; the target never contains the dummy. The resulting coefficient is binom(a,r) 2^r (b)_r/(n)_{2r} for either parity.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: This is an exact implication for all allowable sizes, not only the full-matching specialization or a Poisson approximation. Exchangeability supplies the uniform model regardless of matching geometry, and hypergeometric thinning supplies the finite formula. The partial-permutation sources concern bipartite assignments or omitted domains and are not needed for the implication.

originality.rationale: Deng's earlier Lemma 3.3 and Theorem 1.2 cover the mathematically substantive matching claims by fixed-size thinning of a uniform perfect matching. The exact PGF follows by thinning the perfect-matching overlap count against a single disjoint-edge target. The fixed-q joint conditional Poisson law follows by exposing replicates in order with the previous partial matchings as bounded-degree targets and then thinning. The Gaussian size limit is the interval local-minimum limit with a bounded change at the seam; the Gaussian–Poisson product is the usual conditioning consequence of the conditional limit having a constant limit law. The finite shared-replicate covariance is a direct law-of-total-covariance specialization of the edge marginals and size variance. The distribution-free calibration is a useful interpretation, but follows immediately by transitivity and does not make these implications new. This decision is based on actual earlier results and their implications, not a same-day similarity or an inaccessible paper.
residual_risks: The exact conditional-calibration wording was not found verbatim in an independent record, but the mathematical finite law and joint limit follow by the documented reductions. No same-day priority assumed. The mirror miss for e852fe58266d is not material to the adverse decision.

value.rationale: The inference problem is meaningful: conditioning on observed sizes gives an exact nuisance-free null calibration for whether a reciprocal pair persists under independent resampling. Simultaneous asymptotics explain why a real finite shared-replicate dependence can vanish, and when size fluctuations separate from the overlap statistics. This is usefulness of the benchmark, not credit for a new mathematical contribution beyond the sources and implications assessed above.
residual_risks: The calibration assumes independent occasions, not a longitudinal or correlated null. The residual covariance computation itself is routine; neither it nor an application framing justifies a repaired novelty claim.
